instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl with 1/2 tsp salt and whisk until no streaks are left. Set aside.
Dice the onion and the tomatoes. Cut 1 jalapeno in half, scrape out the seeds and dice it small. Mince the garlic. Slice the other jalapeno and put it in a small bowl for the table.

Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and the diced jalapeno with a pinch of salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and clear.
Add the garlic, 1 tsp of the berbere and the cardamom. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, until they're soft and most of their juice has cooked off.
Turn the heat to low and add the last 1 tbsp butter. When it melts, pour in the eggs.
Fold the eggs slowly from the edges to the middle with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat while they're still soft and glossy. They'll finish cooking in the pan.
Put the last 1 tsp of berbere in a second small bowl for the table.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with injera, with the sliced jalapeno and the berbere at the table.
method_notes: Enkulal tibs is the egg dish in the tibs style, fried quickly in butter with onion and chili. Only one write-up by name was readable (the Global Veggie one, no rating, and a plain omelette with bell pepper, cardamom, garlic and ginger), and the Tropics Gourmet page could not be opened. So this follows the better-known enkulal firfir cooks (Ethiopian Food Guide, 5.0 from 4 ratings, and Fork and Salt, no rating) for the onion, tomato, jalapeno and berbere in spiced butter, and cooks the eggs soft rather than set. Niter kibbeh is hard to find, so plain butter plus berbere and cardamom stands in. The jalapeno seeds are out and the extra heat goes on the side.
